land.text: the Ye land, reorganized into Lintun Commandery in 108 BCE and independent in 82 BCE

predecessors.note: Lintun (107-82 BCE) is Han land that Cliopatria draws no row for; the Gojoseon (Wiman Joseon) dossier records that the Ye were Wiman Joseon's subjects before Han.

land.text: the Ye land, annexed by Gwanggaeto

successors.note: The page dates the annexation to the 'early 5th-century'; Cliopatria's Goguryeo shape already holds the land from 392. A small southern part went to Silla (page: no year, no place), left out of this handover.

capitals.name: Haslla (Gangneung)
capitals.note: The page calls Haslla (present-day Gangneung) 'originally capital of Ye' (a footnote, no year); it is the only seat named, so it is held for the whole life.

correction.text: the same shape, held from -82 only: 'reorganized into Lintun Commandery(108 BC)' and 'Become independent in 82 BC'; for -91..-83 the land is Han's Lintun Commandery

keyframe_review.note: -91..-37, 25,776 km2. The page's territory is 'South Hamgyŏng and Kangwon provinces in North Korea and Gangwon in South Korea' and it gives no area, so the infobox comparison is not possible; the Cliopatria shape (lat 36.8-39.1N) is a core of that. Years change, not the outline: the state begins in 82 BCE, nine years after Cliopatria's row, and the earlier years belong to Han (counterpart han-dynasty, who has no row for Lintun).

-36..312, 29,016 km2, 3,240 km2 larger than the -91 shape from the year Cliopatria also starts Dong-okjeo (-36). No page explains the growth. The page says Ye 'appears in history as a vassal state of Goguryeo' and the Goguryeo page that Taejo (reign 53-146) conquered 'the Dongye and other tribes', neither dated; the dossier does not change the shape for it and the Goguryeo dossier should carry the vassal_start. Unverified: page budget.

313..382, 29,045 km2 (+29 km2): the year Goguryeo absorbed Lelang ('the last Chinese commandery at Lelang was conquered and absorbed by Micheon in 313', Goguryeo page). The change is a boundary adjustment at the Lelang frontier, not a gain or loss on any page opened.
383..386, 29,068 km2 (+23 km2). No page dates anything on the Ye coast in these years; the variation is boundary noise at the neighbours' edges. Unverified: page budget.
387..389, 29,045 km2 (-23 km2). Unverified: page budget; same outline as 313.

390..391, 29,045 km2. Cliopatria ends Dongye here and gives the land to Goguryeo from 392 (Goguryeo 216,216 km2, +31,200 km2), the year after Gwanggaeto's accession in 391; the Eastern Ye page says instead 'In early 5th-century, however, King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo annexed Ye', so the shape is carried on in the next keyframe.

correction.text: the 390 shape carried on, because the page dates the annexation to 'early 5th-century', not 391; the end year 401 is the earliest year that fits the page

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 392-401, years the Cliopatria row lacks (the Goguryeo row holds the land from 392). 401 is the dossier's bridging choice (confidence 1) within 'early 5th-century'; the Gwanggaeto page (reign from 391) does not mention Ye or the east coast, so it cannot narrow it. A reviewer may prefer 391 to match Cliopatria's Goguryeo.

region.text: the Ye land of 'South Hamgyŏng and Kangwon provinces in North Korea and Gangwon in South Korea'

ledger.note: 82 BCE: the Ye become independent of Han as Lintun is abolished. 'With the establishment of Four Commanderies of Han, it was reorganized into Lintun Commandery(108 BC)'; footnote: 'Become independent in 82 BC'. The Four Commanderies page: 'In 82 BCE, Lintun was absorbed into Xuantu and Zhenfan absorbed into Lelang'. The page dates the Ye chiefdom itself only to 'roughly 3rd-century BC'; Cliopatria begins the row in 91 BCE.

401: Goguryeo annexes the Ye. 'In early 5th-century, however, King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo annexed Ye, leading to Goguryeo's domination of the entire northern portion of the Korean peninsula and most of Manchuria.' The page gives no year; 401 is the first year of the century, inside Gwanggaeto's reign (391-413, Goguryeo page). A small southern part is said to have gone to Silla, also without a year.

wars.name: Ye attacks on the southern neighbours (AD 40 and AD 60)
wars.outcome: Raids with no territorial result on the page.
wars.note: Footnote 2: 'In AD 40, September, people from Hwaryeo and Bulnaeye joined forces to lead cavalry and invade the northern frontier' (the footnote does not name whose frontier); footnote 1: 'In AD 60, the Siljik king fled to Uljin when Haslla attacked the Siljikgok.' Hwaryeo, Bulnaeye and Haslla are Ye statelets on the page. Month 9 of AD 40; no border moved.

wars.name: Goguryeo's subjugation of the Okjeo and Dongye (reign of Taejo)
wars.outcome: Goguryeo made the Okjeo tributary and took the Ye as a vassal; the sentences are undated.
wars.note: Goguryeo page: 'Taejo conquered the Okjeo tribes of what is now northeastern Korea as well as the Dongye and other tribes' (no date; reign 53-146); Okjeo page: 'King Taejo of Goguryeo reduced Okjeo to a tributary'; Eastern Ye: Ye 'appears in history as a vassal state of Goguryeo'. No zone because the Ye kept their land. The vassal_start belongs in the Goguryeo dossier (counterpart dongye) once a page dates it.

wars.name: Goguryeo's annexation of Ye under Gwanggaeto
wars.outcome: Goguryeo annexed the Ye; the page puts it in the early 5th century and adds that a small southern part was absorbed into Silla.
wars.note: The span is Gwanggaeto's reign (Gwanggaeto page: his reign began in 391 and Jangsu succeeded him; 391-413 on the Goguryeo page). The Gwanggaeto page lists campaigns of 398 (Sushen), 400 (Silla's rescue) and 410 (Eastern Buyeo) but none against Ye. No contest event: no page dates a front.

certainty.note: A chiefdom confederation on the east coast with no treaty or survey line on any page; the Cliopatria outline is a core of the three modern provinces the page names.

sources.title: Dongye
sources.note: A disambiguation page (Eastern Ye, and three places named Dongye in China); the article of Cliopatria's 'Dongye' is Eastern Ye.

sources.title: Eastern Ye
sources.note: Identity, territory, 128-82 BCE footnotes, Haslla, the AD 40 and 60 raids, annexation by Goguryeo in the 'early 5th-century'. A short page; the Wikipedia title 'Dongye' is a disambiguation page.

sources.title: Four Commanderies of Han
sources.note: Lintun 107-82 BCE absorbed into Xuantu; Nan Lü of Dongye surrendering to Han.

sources.title: Okjeo
sources.note: Okjeo bordering Dongye on the south; Taejo made Okjeo tributary.

sources.title: Goguryeo
sources.note: Taejo's conquest of the Okjeo and Dongye (undated, reign 53-146); Lelang absorbed in 313.

sources.title: Gwanggaeto the Great
sources.note: Reign from 391; campaigns of 398, 400, 402 and 410; no mention of Ye.

notes: Cliopatria's Wikipedia field 'Dongye' is a disambiguation page; the article is 'Eastern Ye' (identity.wikipedia). The Ye chiefdom is dated by the page only to 'roughly 3rd-century BC to around early 5th-century AD', so the dossier starts at the one dated event, independence in 82 BCE (footnote 1), and the keyframe -91 is shortened: Cliopatria's -91..-83 years are Han's Lintun Commandery (reorganized 108 BCE; Four Commanderies page: Lintun 107-82 BCE). Pre-state history from the pages, not in the ledger because it falls before the start: 129 BCE 'It belonged to the Wiman Joseon', and 'NamRyeo, the leader of Yemaek, betrayed the Wiman Joseon and belongs to the Han Dynasty in 128 BC' (Eastern Ye footnote 1); the Four Commanderies page calls Nan Lü 'a monarch of Dongye and a subject of Wiman Chosŏn' who surrendered to Han with 280,000 people, after which a Canghai Commandery was set up and abolished within two years. The end is the weak point: the page says Gwanggaeto annexed Ye in the 'early 5th-century' and a small southern part went to Silla (no year, no place), while Cliopatria ends the row in 391 and starts Goguryeo's 216,216 km2 shape in 392 (which includes the Ye land). The dossier ends in 401 at confidence 1; the Goguryeo dossier should date its gain of the Ye consistently (or the reviewer should pick 391). Goguryeo's vassalage of the Ye (Taejo, reign 53-146) is undated on every page opened, so no vassal_start is recorded here; it belongs in the Goguryeo dossier with counterpart dongye. The Cliopatria Korean Jin shape (to -92) contains the Ye land, which the pages do not support: see the korean-jin dossier. No infobox area exists on any page; the territory (South Hamgyong, Kangwon, Gangwon) is larger than the 25-29 thousand km2 shape. The 23-29 km2 shape variations of 313-390 are boundary noise. Page budget: 5 pages of 5 (the Dongye disambiguation page not counted).
